text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 18 in history.
1189 - William II, last Norman king of Sicily, died and was succeeded by Tancred the Bastard.
1477 - William Caxton produced the first printed book in the English language, The Dictes and Sayengis of the Phylosophers.
1852 - The state funeral of the Duke of Wellington, statesman, diplomat and commander-in-chief of the British Army, took place in London.
1860 - Polish pianist Ignacy Jan Paderewski born. Noted for his interpretaions of Schubert and Chopin, he became prime minister of Poland in 1919 and president in 1940.
1883 - The United States adopted standard time, the country henceforth to be divided into four time-zones.
1886 - Chester Alan Arthur, 21st U.S. president (1881-84), died.
1903 - Panama and the United States signed a treaty on the proposed Panama Canal.
1905 - Prince Charles of Denmark was elected first king of Norway after the restoration of its independence. He took the old Norse name of Haakon VII.
1918 - The Latvian National Council proclaimed the independent Republic of Latvia, with Janis Cakste as president.
1918 - The Belgian army reoccupied Brussels after four years of German occupation.
1923 - Alan Shepard, the first American in space (1961), born.
1928 - Walt Disney's Mickey Mouse made his first appearance at the Colony Theatre in New York in a film called "Steamboat Willie".
1935 - Economic sanctions imposed on Italy by the League of Nations for her invasion of Abyssinia (Ethiopia) took effect.
1936 - Germany under Adolf Hitler and Italy under Benito Mussolini both recognised General Francisco Franco's provisional government in Spain.
1941 - John Watson, Australia's first Labor prime minister, died.
1945 - The communist-led Fatherland Front won the Bulgarian general election after opposition parties abstained.
1969 - Joseph P. Kennedy, diplomat, ambassador and father of John F., Robert and Edward, died.
1978 - The Reverend Jim Jones, a U.S. pastor, led 914 followers to their deaths at Jonestown, Guyana by drinking a cyanide-laced fruit drink. Cult members who refused to swallow the liquid were shot.
1987 - 30 people died at Kings Cross station on the London Underground in a fire which started on a wooden escalator.
1991 - British peace envoy Terry Waite and U.S. academic Thomas Sutherland were released from five years of captivity in Lebanon by Islamic Jihad.
1992 - Police arrested Pakistani opposition leader Benazir Bhutto amid clouds of teargas when she tried to lead a "long march" on parliament house to demand the government's removal.

1993 - Black and white leaders in South Africa approved the new democracy constitution which gave blacks the vote and ended white minority rule. It was signed by President F.W. de Klerk and Nelson Mandela, president of the African National Congress.
1993 - Ukraine's parliament overwhelmingly ratified the START-1 disarmament treaty but placed stiff conditions on giving up the former Soviet nuclear weapons on its territory.
1995 - The Vatican said the Roman Catholic ban on the ordination of women as priests was a definitive, infallible and unquestionable part of the Church's doctrine.
